pairs.locus: Augustine, De Civitate Dei 8.23 (Hermes/Asclepius, Asclepius Latinus)
pairs.question: Statuas dicis, o Trismegiste?
pairs.answer: Statuas, o Asclepi, uides quatenus tu ipse diffidas; statuas animatas sensu et spiritu plenas tantaque facientes et talia, statuas futurorum praescias eaque sorte uate somniis multisque aliis rebus praedicentes, inbecillitates hominibus facientes easque curantes, tristitiam laetitiamque pro meritis.
pairs.derivation: Direct-speech exchange quoted by Augustine from the Hermetic Asclepius. Question: dropped the asking-narration framing 'Hic cum Asclepius, ad quem maxime loquebatur, ei respondisset atque dixisset:' and kept Asclepius's verbatim utterance. Answer: dropped the reply-tag 'tum ille:' and the inline framing 'inquit' (narration of speaking) from 'Statuas, inquit, o Asclepi...'. The answer affirms and elaborates the question (yes, statues, and what they are). Cut the answer at the first full stop after 'tristitiam laetitiamque pro meritis.'; what follows ('An ignoras, o Asclepi, quod Aegyptus imago sit caeli...') turns from answering to a digression on Egypt as image of heaven, so it is excluded.
